recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It fixes a stale active source row that feeds primitive type definitions while preserving later approved decimal exponent behavior and existing precision documentation.
issue_request: FHIR-5653 was Published with a Persuasive with Modification resolution for FHIR-core datatypes. It requested clarification that decimal is not the full domain of rational numbers, explanation of precision-aware decimal handling relative to XSD decimal/precisionDecimal, and clearer exponent language.
initial_application: The main datatypes page appears to have been initially updated by the 2015 primitive datatype rewrite: commit 7b5ff8e added the phrase 'Rational numbers that have a decimal representation' and precision guidance shortly after the Jira was filed. Current source/datatypes.html still carries that clarified narrative, but source/datatypes/primitives.xml retained the older 'A rational number with implicit precision' generated-definition wording and a Java BigInteger implementation example.
additional_context: FHIR-8175 later confirmed the same precision-aware decimal design while leaving schema mapping in place. FHIR-16874 later allowed exponential form in all formats, so the current xs:decimal/xs:double union and exponent-capable regex should be preserved rather than reverting to FHIR-5653's original exponent-prohibition concern.
reconciliation: Changed source/datatypes/primitives.xml so the decimal Definition cell now says 'A rational number that has a decimal representation, with implicit precision' and the Comments cell names Java BigDecimal instead of Java BigInteger. No changes were made to exponent handling.
source_changes: source/datatypes/primitives.xml: updated the decimal Definition and Comments cells to align generated primitive type source with the current datatypes narrative and BigDecimal guidance.

related_jiras.note: Same decimal precision/XSD family; confirms precision-aware decimal handling should be documented while leaving schema mapping in place.
Later published datatypes decision allowed exponential form in all formats, so the old exponent prohibition should not be restored.
